plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch covariate
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single raw integer count matrix from salmon (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 12 human kidney samples, gene symbols in the first column) plus a 12 x 3 sample table (metadata.csv) carrying condition (treated vs control, 6 each) and batch (two processing batches, each holding both conditions). The research question is purely which genes differ between treated and control, so the plan stops at a differential expression result and its report — no enrichment step is added, since the user did not ask for pathways.

Because the batch is known and balanced across conditions, it enters the design formula as a fixed effect (~ batch + condition) rather than being removed from the counts beforehand; adjusting counts and then testing them would report confidence the data does not support. Step T1S1 runs sample structure QC on a blind VST — PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and library sizes — coloured by both condition and batch, so the relative size of the batch effect and any outlier sample is visible before any test. T1S2 fits the model: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside DESeq2, Wald test for the condition contrast (treated vs control, control explicitly set as the denominator), apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. With 6 replicates per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers and sets their p-values to NA rather than replacing counts, so those genes are counted and reported separately from genes lost to independent filtering. T1S3 refits the same counts and the same design with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test; at 6 replicates per group the two tools agree on most genes but not all, so the intersection is the high-confidence set and the method-specific calls are a secondary set. T1S4 assembles the report: MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, the gene table with unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold changes and lfcSE, the two-method overlap, and the full reproducibility record.

The design is small (n=6 per group) and the matrix is pre-quantified at gene level, so the honest scope is a ranked, FDR-controlled gene table with an explicit statement of how many genes were tested and how many passed — not a mechanistic claim.

Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples (smallest group size)
~ batch + condition with explicit reference level control
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as second method for robustness overlap
Report with MA plot, dispersion plot, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, sessionInfo
